newsitem.title: USA: Film company to make TV movie on U.S. suicide cult.
newsitem.headline: Film company to make TV movie on U.S. suicide cult.

text.p: An independent film company, Kushner-Locke, said on Thursday it had signed a deal with the ABC television network to produce a made-for-television movie about the Heaven's Gate cult based on a personal account of a former member, Rio D'Angelo.

D'Angelo, who left the cult just four weeks before the other 39 members in the group took their lives, is the one who discovered the scene of the mass suicide and made a videotape of the dead bodies before notifying police.
"His story will give our audience the most thorough and thoughtful understanding of what was going on," said Kushner-Locke co-chairman Peter Locke.

Shortly after leaving the cult, D'Angelo received a Federal Express package containing the farewell video from members. With a friend, he drove to the group's home in Rancho Santa Fe, where he found their bodies.

Kushner-Locke first became involved with the Heaven's Gate cult when it hired some of its members to design its World Wide Web site on the Internet. It will produce the movie in association with InterAct Entertainment, where D'Angelo is employed.
ABC is a unit of Walt Disney Co.
